summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Galle International Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as New Zealand posted 249/10 (83.2 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 267/10 (93.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: A Dananjaya (6/80), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, FDM Karunaratne delivered a masterclass for Sri Lanka (161 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Sri Lanka 47%) and allowing Sri Lanka to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, New Zealand faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Sri Lanka's bowling unit, bolstered by AY Patel (14 Runs & 6 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Sri Lanka won by 6 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Sri Lanka's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While New Zealand produced fighting phases, Sri Lanka won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
